questions.q: What does it mean that Python is an interpreted language?
options: The interpreter reads and runs the code directly, with no separate compile step
The code must be compiled into a .exe before it can run
It only runs inside a web browser
It translates Python into Java before running
questions.explain: Python code runs directly through the interpreter, unlike compiled languages.

questions.q: Why do data engineers favor Python specifically for pipeline work?
options: It has mature, well-tested libraries for every pipeline step: files, APIs, databases, and reshaping data
It is the only language capable of reading a CSV file
It runs faster than every compiled language
It is required by every database vendor
questions.explain: Libraries like pandas, requests, and pyodbc are why Python became the default glue language for pipelines.

questions.q: What is the key difference between the REPL and a saved script?
options: The REPL runs lines immediately but saves nothing when closed; a script is saved and can be run the same way repeatedly
The REPL and a script behave identically in every way
A script can only contain comments, not real code
The REPL is used for production pipelines, scripts are only for testing
questions.explain: Real, repeatable pipelines must live in saved files, not be retyped into an interactive prompt.

questions.q: What does a comment do in Python?
options: Nothing — the interpreter ignores it entirely; it exists for human readers
It runs as a lower-priority instruction
It must be removed before the script can run
It changes how fast the script executes
questions.explain: Comments are for the next person reading the code, not for the interpreter.

questions.q: How do you run a saved script named pipeline.py from the terminal?
options: python pipeline.py
run pipeline.py
pipeline.py --execute
open pipeline.py
questions.explain: The python command followed by the filename is how scripts are executed from the terminal.
